question: Broadly shared: progression to dementia within four years among patients at the MCI stage, predicted from clinical/cognitive data (both papers have a clinical-feature model) and, secondarily, MRI volumes. P-274 uses BioFINDER-1 SCD/MCI with CSF-confirmed AD dementia as the outcome, plus an ADNI MCI external subset. P-192 uses ADNI amnestic MCI with clinical dementia 'not necessarily due to AD' as the outcome. The cohort, the inclusion of SCD, the outcome definition and the training design differ: P-192 trains CN-vs-dementia classifiers and applies them to aMCI. The rule allows these as candidate explanations. Condition 1 is arguable rather than clearly failed, and the pair fails on condition 2 in any case.
metric: Mismatch. P-274 reports ROC-AUC (and MCC). P-192 reports no AUC and no accuracy for the MCI progression task, only threshold-dependent sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV at each follow-up. The recorded 'PPV 68%' depends on prevalence and threshold, AUC depends on neither, and no value of one excludes a value of the other.

figures.P-274: Four-year progression to AD dementia, BioFINDER-1 test sets (n = 332, 109 progressors). Clinical data model AUC 0.850 (CI 0.698-0.954). Clinical + intracranial and hippocampal volume AUC 0.862 (CI 0.728-0.960). ADNI MCI external subset (n = 108): FreeSurfer 0.688, DL 0.799.
figures.P-192: ADNI aMCI (n = 415), CN-vs-dementia RUSBoost/LR classifiers applied at a 0.5 cut-off. At 4 years: biomarker RUSBoost PPV 68% against an observed incidence of 22.2%, sensitivity 61.5%, specificity 91.7%. Clinical feature set RUSBoost PPV 67.3%, sensitivity 63.4%, specificity 91.2%. No AUC, no accuracy and no interval printed for these.

matched_figure_check: No matched figure exists on a common metric. P-192 prints no AUC for the MCI progression task, and P-274 prints no sensitivity, specificity or PPV. Converting between them would need the full ROC curve or the operating point, which neither paper supplies.
performance_validity: The exclusion does not apply. No value reaches 0.97 (P-274 0.862; P-192's specificities of 91-92% are threshold-dependent rates, not discrimination). Not a comparable performance pair. Checked against P-274 page 6 and P-192 pages 4-5 and 11-13.
reason: Even granting the broad clinical question (four-year progression to dementia from the MCI stage, clinical-data channel), the two papers report different metric types. P-274 reports AUC. P-192 reports only sensitivity, specificity and PPV at a fixed cut-off, and its headline PPV depends on the 22% incidence in ADNI. The ledger's 'gap' of 0.18 subtracts a PPV from an AUC. Condition 2 fails, and no discrepancy can be read from the printed figures.

quotes.quote: The primary binary outcome was four-year progression to AD dementia, where a clinical diagnosis of AD dementia during the four years follow-up was considered as a progression.
Adding intracranial and hippocampal volume to the clinical data model increased the test AUC to 0.862 (CI 0.728–0.960)
> 45% over 4 years (model’s PPV = 68% vs. observed rate of dementia onset = 22.2%)
dementia diagnosis was not necessarily due to AD, and we did not exclude subjects based on presence or absence of AD pathology.
Sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and negative predictive value (NPV) for each model were calculated.
Using baseline data from CN and dementia participants, a LR model was trained to differentiate participants with dementia from healthy controls.
